title: Primary User Interview Protocol: First-Year SIP Retention & Lapse Discovery
methodology: Teresa Torres Story-Based Interview Protocol (Strictly Empathy & Problem Space)
target_cohort: First-time retail investors in India who initiated a mutual fund SIP but paused, cancelled, or lapsed within 12 months
core_rules: Never ask speculative questions ('Would you use a feature that...?').
Anchor questions in specific past events ('Tell me about the last time you paused or stopped your SIP.').
Listen for emotional keywords: worry, anger, surprise, confusion, relief.

interview_tracks.objective: Understand the initial expectation and emotional anchor at the moment of starting
questions: Think back to the day you set up your first SIP. Where were you, and what made you decide to do it that day?
What did you expect would happen to that money after 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year?
Who did you talk to or what did you watch before hitting the confirm button?
interview_tracks.confirmation_criteria: User articulates a specific external trigger (friend, influencer, tax season) and expects steady non-volatile capital growth.
interview_tracks.invalidation_criteria: User had professional financial advisory and entered with calibrated expectations of 3-year volatility.

interview_tracks.objective: Uncover behavioral habits and early disillusionment
questions: Walk me through the first time you opened the app to check your portfolio after the installment was deducted. What did you see?
How did you feel about the numbers on the screen compared to what you had in mind?
How often did you find yourself checking the app in month two and month three?
interview_tracks.confirmation_criteria: User experienced 'underwhelming returns shock' and checked frequently before dropping off into app silence.
interview_tracks.invalidation_criteria: User set-and-forgot the SIP completely without looking at the screen.

interview_tracks.objective: Pinpoint the exact catalyst that broke the monthly installment cadence
questions: Tell me about the specific month when your SIP was first missed, paused, or cancelled.
What was happening with your finances that week?
Did you actively decide to stop it, or did an auto-debit failure or bank penalty happen first?
Once it stopped, what went through your mind about restarting it?
interview_tracks.confirmation_criteria: Lapse was driven by either cash flow mismatch, bank bounce penalty dread, or disappointment with stagnant returns.
interview_tracks.invalidation_criteria: Lapse was purely due to deliberate profit booking after reaching a designated financial goal.

interview_tracks.objective: Identify moments where technical or UX ambiguity caused distress
questions: Did you ever see a situation where money left your bank account, but your Zerodha Coin portfolio didn't show the units right away? What did you do?
Did you ever try to pause, skip, or edit your SIP amount? What happened when you tried?
Did you reach out to customer support? How did that go?
interview_tracks.confirmation_criteria: User felt trapped or bewildered by T+2 Demat delays, Coin vs AMC SIP restrictions, or unhelpful support tickets.
interview_tracks.invalidation_criteria: User found settlement mechanics transparent and effortless.
